page: Amazon Web Services d3.4xlarge is a dense storage instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading, running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. A key characteristic of this server is its massive local storage capacity, consisting of 23760 GB of HDD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by bottom-quartile results in stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores falling within the middle 50% category. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also demonstrate average performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the d3.4xlarge offers high resource density specifically for storage-heavy workloads, trading off high-speed solid-state performance for massive, lower-cost HDD capacity. The instance is well-suited for workloads requiring large-scale sequential data access, such as distributed file systems, data lakes, log processing, and big data analytics. It is less optimal for compute-intensive or single-threaded tasks that do not leverage its storage capacity.
